name: Engineering & Process Explainer 3D
description: Master 3D template for physical, mechanical, and architectural explainers. Full progressive timeline animations (dig, pour, fill, drain, collapse, buoyancy, insert) in persistent cutaway cross-section dioramas (earth strata, foundations, piping, structural framing) rather than simple isometric idle loops. Supports 5 core engineering archetypes: como-funciona (mechanisms & fluids), paso-a-paso (sequential construction & assembly), que-paso (structural failure forensics), para-que-sirve (hidden components & relief valves), and fuerzas-ingenieria (hydrostatic & physical force vectors). No emoji.
prompt_hint: 5-8 scenes (4-8 s) explaining how a real engineering system, physical structure, or failure happens. EVERY scene: visual.type "scene3d" within a PERSISTENT cutaway world (lawn/ground, strata cutaway with bedrock, pipes, foundations) that stays consistent across the video. Use state-transition timeline motions instead of loops: `dig` (excavation), `pour` (pouring concrete or liquid), `fill` (water level rising), `drain` (emptying), `collapse` (unreinforced walls crumbling), `buoyancy` (hydrostatic upward flotation of empty structures), `insert` (valves and components snapping into place). Include technical overlays (flow strips, concept pills, limit bars) and force indicators. Captions at the bottom. No emoji.
best_for: failure forensics (what happened / why it failed)
fluid dynamics, valves, and piping networks
